name: Corona Remedies Ltd
title: Corona Remedies Ltd - 544644 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue +22.2% to INR441 cr with EBITDA margin flat at 21.7%; management reiterated 1.5x IPM revenue guidance but declined to restate 15%-style numbers and said no MR additions until FY28.

summary.headline: Corona Remedies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores, with PAT up 15.3% to INR60 crores as D&A weighed.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 22.2% YoY to INR441 crores in Q2 FY27 and 22% in H1, with India business at 97% of revenue and 22.9% growth in Q2. EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR96 crores at a stable 21.7% margin, while PAT grew 15.3% to INR60 crores, held back by higher depreciation and amortisation from new facilities and acquired brands. Management reiterated guidance of 1.5x IPM growth (revenue about 15%) and PAT growth of about 20%, and said Wokadine integration and business-model change is running slower than expected. Infertility is the first new therapy push, with a 46-person task force reaching about INR7 lakh PCPM.

financial_highlights.change: +22.2% YoY vs INR361 crores in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Q2 INR12.6 crores; H1 INR25.3 crores

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed 97% of revenue in Q2 and H1, growing 22.9% in Q2 vs about 12% for the Indian pharma market. Chronic portfolio grew about 29% vs 14.9% for the chronic market segment.

segments.name: Engine brands
segments.commentary: 33 engine brands contribute about 79-80% of India business and are growing about 22%. Management aims to build further brands to INR100 crores-plus.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Export revenue was INR12.6 crores in Q2 and INR25.3 crores in H1. Management expects about INR60-65 crores this year and about 15% growth next year; international to stay under 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Wokadine (acquired from Bayer)
segments.commentary: Commercialised this year; base sales maintained in Q2, but integration and business-model change are slower than expected. Management still targets 25% CAGR over 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: Revenue guidance remains 1.5x IPM growth, which management equates to about 15% revenue growth assuming IPM at about 10%.
PAT guided to grow about 20%; no guidance given on operating margins, though margins are expected to improve in coming years after the 400+ MR addition.
IPM expected to grow low double digits (about 10-12%) over the next 3-4 quarters, per management's own view.
International revenue expected at INR60-65 crores this year, growing about 15% next year.
Hormone dossiers (10-12) to be filed over 2-3 years; registrations take 1-2 years after that.
No MR additions planned in CY27; possible addition of about 150 MRs in FY28.
capex_capacity: MR force at 3,111 medical representatives after about 400 added in Q4 FY26; no additions planned until FY28.

IVF task force of 46 people covers about 2,500 infertility professionals and gynaecologists (about 60 per rep), reaching about 75-80% of the market; PCPM about INR7 lakh in first 6 months, targeting INR8-9 lakh by year-end.
Newly commissioned facilities and acquired brands drove higher D&A in the quarter.
Hormone API backward integration via stake in La Chandra; forward integration through a plant in Ahmedabad.
demand_pricing: Indian pharma market grew about 12% in Q2 per PharmaTrac; September 2026 was the market's highest monthly growth at 13.5%, increasingly volume-led.
Over 3 years Corona grew 1.9x the market, with volume growth about 3.3x, new introductions about 2.2x and price about 1.2x the market.
Price growth in the 8.5-8.9% range in recent quarters vs about 5-5.5% historically; management cites NELM/non-NELM mix and market absorption.
Market share: about 0.77% of IPM; 2.3% in core therapies, which grow about 25% faster than IPM. Ranked 26th in the Indian pharma market; 14th among covered companies.
NLEM exposure about 7.5% of revenue (down from 9%); top-5 brand SKUs have 0% under NLEM. Management sees no impact yet from trade margin caps.
Semaglutide: Corona is in the top 10 semaglutide companies; management expects a INR1,200-1,400 crore molecule market in year one; focus stays on engine brands.
No change in competitive intensity observed from smaller branded players or alternate channels.

qa_highlights.question: How is the new therapy strategy (nephrology, CNS, rheumatology, derma) being executed, and is M&A considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Infertility is the first new therapy, with a task force formed in CY2026. Management is open to both organic and inorganic routes and is evaluating proposals, with nothing concrete yet.

qa_highlights.question: How has the Wokadine acquisition performed, and what is growth ex-Wokadine?
qa_highlights.answer: Base sales maintained in Q2 after full distribution and supply-chain integration. Business-model change is slower than expected; next two quarters give more visibility. Ex-Wokadine growth is 21.5% in Q2 and H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no operating-margin guidance. FY26 EBITDA margin was 20.9%, and margins are expected to improve in coming years after the 400+ MR addition.

qa_highlights.question: How is IVF scale-up progressing, and is the team being expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: The 46-person team reached about INR7 lakh PCPM in 6 months, with INR8-9 lakh targeted by year-end. No expansion in CY27; possible in H2 CY27 or early FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 15% revenue guidance be revised given stronger IPM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance remains 1.5x IPM. Management said upside exists if IPM stays at 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for international business and hormones?
qa_highlights.answer: Preparing 10-12 hormone dossiers for regulated and semi-regulated markets, with 2-3 years to revenue. International is about 15% growth this year; less than 10% of revenue in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is price growth higher, and what is the plan for new therapy share?
qa_highlights.answer: Price growth is about 8.5-8.9% vs about 5-5.5% historically, driven by market absorption and NELM/non-NELM mix. Management expects new therapies to enter within 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory risk from price controls and trade margin caps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the pricing matter sub judice and declined detail. NLEM exposure is about 7.5% of revenue; trade margin caps are seen as a trade-channel issue with no impact so far.

risks_watch: Wokadine integration and business-model change are behind plan; the next two quarters will show whether the 25% CAGR target holds.
D&A from new facilities and acquired brands is compressing PAT growth (15.3%) below revenue growth (22.2%).
Pricing and regulatory exposure: NLEM and trade-margin-cap scrutiny; management called the matter sub judice.
International growth was soft in H1; the 15% growth target depends on dossier filings and registrations.
IPM growth is strong now; management expects it to ease to low double digits, which would narrow the upside to the 1.5x guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on core India growth and market outperformance, with specific figures. Noticeably cautious and hedged on Wokadine, international timelines, and IPM outlook (described as a "gut feel"), and evasive on margin guidance and valuation multiples.
key_quotes: We have never given guidance on operating margins, right?
The integration and change in business model are a little slower than expected.
So the estimation of 1.5x in the IPM has always been a guidance, and it will remain as the guidance as far as revenue is concerned.
So these 33 brands are potential INR 100 crores-plus brands, and we are working on it.

adds.what: MR force at 3,111 medical representatives after about 400 added in Q4 FY26; no further additions planned until FY28
Possible addition of about 150 MRs in FY28

growth.why: Management held revenue guidance at 1.5x IPM (about 15% if IPM ~10%) and PAT growth of about 20%, after Q2 revenue rose 22.2%; backing is partly specific (3,111 MRs, 46-person infertility task force, INR60-65 crore international target) but there is no new capacity commissioned or planned before FY28 and Wokadine integration is running slower than expected.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: No operating-margin guidance; EBITDA margin 21.7% in Q2 and 21.9% in H1 vs FY26 20.9%, with margins expected to improve after the 400+ MR addition, but D&A from new facilities is compressing PAT growth to 15.3% vs revenue 22.2%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: no new MR additions before FY28
rows.why: MR force at 3,111 after about 400 added in Q4 FY26; no additions planned in CY27 and a possible 150 MRs only in FY28, so no new field capacity is due in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India business grew 22.9% in Q2 vs about 12% for the Indian pharma market, with 33 engine brands growing about 22% and volume growth about 3.3x the market over 3 years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given; the only new spend is backward integration via La Chandra and an Ahmedabad forward-integration plant, with no date or amount.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance held at 1.5x IPM (about 15%) and PAT growth of about 20% after Q2 revenue grew 22.2%; management said upside exists if IPM stays at 10-12%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects IPM to ease to low double digits (about 10-12%) over the next 3-4 quarters, which narrows the upside to 1.5x guidance, and Wokadine integration is running behind plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Infertility is the first new therapy with a 46-person task force at about INR7 lakh PCPM targeting INR8-9 lakh by year-end; 10-12 hormone dossiers take 2-3 years to revenue, and no new product launch date is given.

rows.label: Wokadine 25% CAGR target
rows.why: Base sales maintained in Q2 but business-model change is slower than expected; management still targets 25% CAGR over 3-4 years, and the next two quarters give more visibility.

rows.label: International INR60-65 crore FY27
rows.why: Export revenue was INR25.3 crores in H1, so INR60-65 crores for the year needs a steep H2 ramp, and the 15% growth target depends on dossier filings and registrations.

rows.label: NLEM and trade-margin-cap scrutiny
rows.why: NLEM exposure is about 7.5% of revenue and management called the pricing matter sub judice; price growth of 8.5-8.9% vs 5-5.5% historically is a watch item.

tone.note: Management was confident on India outperformance (22.9% vs about 12% market) and the infertility ramp, but cautious on Wokadine, international timelines and IPM outlook, and evasive on margin guidance; analysts pushed on margins, Wokadine performance and the pricing/regulatory risk.
